assessments.reasoning: Both captures of the LaTeX Project's lppl-1-3a.txt, 9b0e698246dd4076be8d9a105f1fa7f5 and 624ad12f25fa48c9a2adcabcf6dc4f52, cover contiguous ranges through EOF. The reconstructed plaintext yielded SHA-256 06403f8c2fd53f994c4a424a8eaa65175062afc96422671f60374f4baf16091a.

challenge.method: Joined bytes [0,16384) and [16384,18435) without a separator and recomputed the full SHA-256. Checked the preamble's “small modifications” wording, model-license guidance, clauses 2, 4 and 11, and the application instructions through the end of the second partition.
challenge.results: The 18435-byte digest matched. The preamble discusses using the license for a non-TeX work. The document header continues to prohibit modification of the LPPL itself. Clauses on a Work and its maintainer give no rights in unrelated works. To apply the license, the author is directed to place a copyright notice and licensing statement in each component. The example says version 1.3 or later and names M. Y. Name as maintainer. Copying it verbatim makes neither choice for an actual work.

limitations: The copied example establishes no actual project's version election, maintenance status, maintainer, or component list.
reasoning: “The LaTeX Project Public License” opens with “LPPL Version 1.3a  2004-10-01” and “Copyright 1999 2002-04 LaTeX3 Project”. The header expressly allows everyone to distribute verbatim copies of this license document and prohibits modifying it. The permission covers the complete file, including the work notice that spans the partition boundary.
